title: Bike for Sale
paragraphs: BIKE FOR SALE! A red mountain bike for a boy or a girl from ten to fourteen years old. It works very well.
The bike is two years old. It has a new chain, a bell and a small light. The seat is soft and comfortable. There is a small scratch on the left side.
A new bike costs $120, but the price of this bike is only $60.
My sister doesn't ride it now because she is very tall. Please call Lucas after five o'clock on 555 0123. You can see the bike at 18 Oak Street, near the bakery.

title: Recycling Day at Our School
paragraphs: RECYCLING DAY at Colegio Nuevo Mundo! Next Saturday, 9 November, from 9:00 to 12:00. Help us make our school clean and green.

Bring your old paper, plastic bottles, cans and glass bottles from home. Put them in the big boxes in the yard. There are four boxes: blue for paper, yellow for plastic, grey for cans and green for glass.
Every student with ten things gets a small plant! There is also a game for children: find the rubbish and put it in the right box. The winner gets a free ticket to the cinema.
Don't bring food or batteries. Remember: recycling is easy, and our planet needs us. Ask Ms Duarte for more information.

title: Where Is My Key?
focus: Present simple; there is / there isn't
paragraphs: Ana is at the front door of her house. She looks in her bag, but she can't find her key. 'Oh no!' she says. 'Where is my key?'
Ana looks in her pockets. There is a pencil, a tissue and a coin, but there is no key. She looks under the mat and behind the flowerpot. No key!
Her neighbour, Mr Gómez, comes with his dog. 'What's the problem, Ana?' he asks. 'I can't find my key,' she says. 'Look at your neck!' says Mr Gómez.
Ana puts her hand on her neck. The key is on a string around her neck! 'I'm so silly!' she laughs. Mr Gómez laughs, too. Now Ana opens the door and goes inside.

title: Emilio, the Young Chef
paragraphs: Emilio Vargas is twelve years old, and he is a very good cook. He lives in Lima with his mother and his two grandparents. His dream is to be a chef.

Emilio cooks on Saturdays and Sundays. Today he is making a Peruvian dish: rice with chicken. First he cuts the vegetables. Then he cooks the chicken in a big pot. His grandmother helps him, but she doesn't tell him what to do.
Emilio can cook ten different dishes. His favourite is ceviche, but he can't make it alone. He needs an adult to help him with the fish. He has a small notebook with all his recipes.
Every Sunday, Emilio's family eats lunch together and Emilio is the chef. 'Cooking is fun!' he says. 'And everyone is happy when they eat!'

title: Swimming Pool Rules
paragraphs: Swimming Pool Rules. Welcome to the Aqua Club pool! Please read these rules. They are for your safety.
Shower before you swim. Wear a swimming cap. Children under eight must be with an adult.
Don't run near the pool. Don't push other people. Don't eat or drink in the water. You can't dive in the shallow end.
Open: Tuesday to Sunday, 8:00 to 6:00. Closed on Mondays. The lifeguard is always at the pool. If you need help, call him!

title: Super Dog and the Ball
focus: Present simple and continuous; there is
paragraphs: Panel 1. In the park, a boy called Tito is playing with his dog, Rayo. Tito: 'Rayo, get the ball!' He throws the red ball.
Panel 2. Rayo runs fast. But the ball is not on the grass. It is in a tree! Rayo: 'Woof? A ball in a tree?'
Panel 3. A cat is sitting in the tree next to the ball. The cat: 'This is my new toy, dog!' Rayo can't climb the tree.
Panel 4. Rayo has an idea. He brings a long stick and pushes the ball down. The cat is angry. 'Hey, give me my toy!'
Panel 5. Tito laughs and gives the cat a small toy mouse. The cat is happy now. Tito: 'Now everybody has a toy. Let's play!'

title: Why I Love Summer
focus: Present simple; adjectives; like / don't like
paragraphs: My favourite season is summer! I'm Laura and I'm from Santiago, in Chile. Summer here is from December to March.
In summer, the days are long and hot. The sky is blue every day. School is closed, so I'm free!
On Saturdays I go to the beach with my family. We swim, play volleyball and eat ice cream. In the evening, we have a barbecue in the garden.
Autumn is nice, too, but it is cold and the days are short. I don't like winter because it rains a lot. What is your favourite season? Why? Tell me in the comments!

title: A Weekend on the Farm
focus: Present simple; there is / there are
paragraphs: Saturday, 14 September. This weekend I'm at my grandma's farm in the mountains. It is very quiet here. There is no traffic and no noise.
In the morning, I help my grandma with the animals. There are five cows, ten chickens and a horse called Trueno. I give the chickens some corn. They are very noisy!
For lunch, we have soup with potatoes from the garden. My grandma makes delicious bread in a clay oven.
In the afternoon, my cousin Iván and I ride the horse. Iván is a good rider, but I am a little scared. In the evening, there are a lot of stars in the sky. I love the farm!

title: Sunny Days English Camp
focus: Present simple; can; numbers and prices
paragraphs: Sunny Days English Camp! Two weeks of English, sport and fun for children from nine to twelve years old. The camp is in the mountains near Cuenca.
Every day starts at 8:00 with a morning song. Then we have English classes with friendly teachers. In the afternoon, children can play football, swim, paint or make a short film.
Children sleep in comfortable cabins with five beds in each. There are three meals a day and two healthy snacks. We also have vegetarian food.
The camp starts on 7 July. The price is $300 and it includes everything. Send an email to info@sunnydays.example or call us. There are only forty places, so write today!
